01 AUG 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah has approved the advance release of ₹2,117.85 crore from the Central share of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) to support the States affected by floods during the ongoing southwest monsoon of 2026. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government remains committed to extending all necessary assistance to States for effective relief, rescue and rehabilitation measures and will continue to monitor the situation closely.

Since the onset of the monsoon, the Government of India has been continuously monitoring the flood situation in close coordination with the State Governments. The Central Government has extended all possible assistance, including pre-deployment of National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and logistical support from the Ministry of Defence, wherever required.

Inter-Ministerial Central Teams (IMCTs) have already been deputed to Arunachal Pradesh and Assam to assess the damages. Two IMCT visits have been undertaken in Assam in view of the severity of the flood situation. On the request of the Government of Nagaland, an IMCT is also being constituted for the State.

Out of the seven affected States, Himachal Pradesh, Odisha and Nagaland have already received the first instalment of SDRF for the financial year 2026-27. In order to ensure timely availability of funds for relief operations, Union Home Minister has approved the advance release of the second instalment of the Central share of SDRF to Himachal Pradesh and Odisha. Further, considering the urgent need for resources for relief measures, advance release of an advance amount of first instalment of the Central share of SDRF has also been approved for Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Gujarat and Maharashtra by relaxing the documentary requirements under the applicable guidelines.

The assistance approved for the affected States includes ₹44.55 crore to Arunachal Pradesh as advance release of the first instalment of the Central share of SDRF for the financial year 2026-27. Assam has been sanctioned ₹379.35 crore as advance release of the first instalment, while Gujarat has been approved ₹500 crore as advance release of the first instalment. Himachal Pradesh, which has already received the first instalment of SDRF for 2026-27, has been sanctioned ₹193.95 crore as advance release of the second instalment of the Central share. Maharashtra has been approved ₹500 crore as advance release of the first instalment. Odisha, which had already received the first instalment, has been sanctioned ₹500 crore as advance release of the second instalment. With this approval, a total of ₹2,117.85 crore has been made available to the flood-affected States to strengthen their ongoing relief and response measures.

headline: NHAI Successfully Launches Multi-Lane Free Flow Tolling System at Shahjahanpur Toll Plaza on the Delhi-Jaipur Section of NH-48
fullText:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways

NHAI Successfully Launches Multi-Lane Free Flow Tolling System at Shahjahanpur Toll Plaza on the Delhi-Jaipur Section of NH-48

Traveling from Manesar to Jaipur becomes barrier-free for the National Highway users

Shahjahanpur becomes the third toll plaza after Daulatpura and Manoharpura to become barrier-free on the busy Delhi-Jaipur Section of NH-48 in Rajasthan

01 AUG 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

In order to provide a faster, seamless and barrier-free travel experience, NHAI has successfully rolled out the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system at Shahjahanpur Toll Plaza on Delhi–Jaipur section of NH-48 in Rajasthan. Earlier, NHAI had rolled out Multi-Lane Free Flow Tolling System at Daulatpura and Manoharpura Toll Plaza on the same corridor. Achieving a significant milestone towards transforming the busy Delhi – Jaipur Section of NH-48, the launch of MLFF at Shahjahanpur Toll Plaza has made traveling from Manesar to Jaipur completely barrier-free and seamless to enhance ‘Ease of Travel’ for the National Highway users.

The MLFF framework introduces barrier-less tolling with minimal human intervention, enabling vehicles to pass through toll locations without stopping and ensuring seamless traffic flow. By enabling zero waiting time and uninterrupted vehicular movement, MLFF has helped commuters to save time, enhance fuel efficiency as well as reduce vehicular emission at the toll location.

The system integrates Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) technology with FASTag-based Electronic Toll Collection to facilitate automated user fee collection. The initiative aligns with the Government of India’s vision of delivering citizen centric services by leveraging technology for enhancing Ease of Living and Ease of Doing Business.

01 AUG 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today presented the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to National Security Advisor Shri Ajit Doval in Pune, Maharashtra. On the occasion, Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Eknath Shinde and Smt. Sunetra Pawar, Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol, along with several other dignitaries, were present.

In his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today marks the 106th death anniversary of Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak. He said that Tilak Maharaj gave the mantra, “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it,” to provide a new direction and meaning to India's freedom struggle. He added that complete Swaraj can be achieved only when our system of governance, language, culture, and religion are firmly established. Shri Shah said that Tilak Maharaj connected the masses with the movements for Swaraj and independence. He further stated that Tilak Maharaj introduced a new form of nationalism—cultural nationalism—into the freedom movement. Shri Shah said that Tilak Maharaj also charted the course the nation would follow in the future, asserting that whenever India attained independence, it would progress along this very path. Today, he said, the country has embarked on the path of cultural nationalism.

Shri Amit Shah said that Lokmanya Tilak was a teacher and an outstanding journalist. As a great thinker, he gave expression to the soul of India before the world and ignited the spirit of Swaraj in the hearts of millions. He said that throughout the freedom movement, there was no one comparable to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak—a visionary, an exceptional teacher, a fearless journalist, a profound thinker, and a Karmayogi.

Union Home Minister said that Tilak Maharaj presented before the nation the practical essence of the Bhagavad Gita. He established a complete educational ecosystem in Pune, beginning with the New English School, followed by the Deccan Education Society, and culminating in Fergusson College. Tilak Maharaj believed that the true purpose of education was to enlighten the intellect with knowledge. Shri Shah said that if the British feared any newspapers, they feared Kesari and The Maratha. He noted that Tilak Maharaj was the first to establish that even if independence were achieved, it would hold little value unless the national consciousness of the people had first been awakened. Tilak Maharaj also emphasized that national strength can never be built without organization and the collective power of the people. Through various public festivals, he united not only the people of Maharashtra but also citizens across the country. Shri Shah further said that self-reliance, discipline, and a sense of duty towards the nation and the Constitution are also integral to Swaraj. He added that the life, thoughts, and writings of Tilak Maharaj continue to serve as a source of inspiration for today's youth and adolescents.

Shri Amit Shah said that today Shri Ajit Doval has been conferred the Lokmanya Tilak National Award. He said that an award is not merely a medal; it is a means of inspiring people and acknowledging the outstanding contributions of eminent individuals. When a person makes an extraordinary contribution in any field of society, he ceases to remain just an individual and rises far above, becoming an enduring source of inspiration. It is the responsibility of society to honour such individuals. He said that by doing so, society not only fulfils its sense of duty but also inspires others to emulate such exemplary personalities. Shri Shah added that the conferment of the Lokmanya Tilak National Award on Shri Ajit Doval will serve as a great source of inspiration for every citizen who lives and works in the service of the nation.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that when Shri Narendra Modi was the Chief Minister of Gujarat, a series of bomb blasts took place in the state. At that time, Shri Narendra Modi had said that the Gujarat Police should investigate not only those bomb blasts but also the individuals involved in them, as well as all the bomb blasts that had occurred across the country. Union Home Minister said that Shri Modi had then directed that Shri Ajit Doval be called to work alongside the Gujarat Police in carrying out the investigation. He added that, as a result, the Gujarat Police succeeded in solving not only the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts but also 13 bomb blast cases from across the country through a coordinated investigation.

Shri Amit Shah said that whenever the history of Shri Narendra Modi's tenure is written and the country's internal and external security is assessed, Shri Ajit Doval will undoubtedly have a golden chapter dedicated to his contributions. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India's foreign policy has become significantly stronger, and the country has firmly established its position in the world with dignity and respect. Shri Shah added that Shri Ajit Doval has made an immense contribution to this achievement of the Modi Government.

Union Home Minister said that from 1972 until he became the Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB), Shri Ajit Doval served as a dedicated Intelligence Bureau officer and played an active role in addressing every major security challenge faced by the country. He said that Shri Doval made extraordinary contributions while serving in the Northeast, Sikkim, Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, and Pakistan, contributions that are beyond description or assessment. He further said that Shri Ajit Doval also served in Pakistan for six years, including during a highly crucial period, making invaluable contributions to the nation's security.

Shri Amit Shah said that after 2019, the Modi Government worked to strengthen the Multi Agency Centre (MAC), which today serves as the backbone of the country's internal security. He said that it was Shri Ajit Doval who laid the strong foundation of the MAC. Shri Shah further said that when Shri Narendra Modi became the Prime Minister of India in 2014, he appointed Shri Ajit Doval as the National Security Advisor. He added that Shri Doval also holds the distinction of being the longest-serving National Security Advisor of the country.

Union Home Minister said that during Shri Ajit Doval's tenure as National Security Advisor, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi took several landmark decisions to modernize India's Armed Forces, introduce contemporary reforms, and achieve an exceptional integration of technology and military prowess within the forces. He said that Shri Doval's extensive experience has been instrumental in shaping many of Prime Minister Modi's decisions. Shri Shah further stated that over the past 12 years, Prime Minister Modi has brought about a transformative change in strengthening the defensive capabilities and offensive preparedness of the Indian Armed Forces, and that Shri Ajit Doval has made a significant contribution to this achievement.

headline: DRI seizes quantities of gold; drugs, e-cigarettes and other contraband in pan-India Ops; 20 persons, including 5 foreign nationals, arrested
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DRI seizes quantities of gold; drugs, e-cigarettes and other contraband in pan-India Ops; 20 persons, including 5 foreign nationals, arrested

01 AUG 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained drive against organised smuggling networks and transnational trafficking syndicates, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has carried out a series of intelligence-led operations across the country during the week, resulting in the seizure of foreign-origin gold, heroin, MDMA, hydroponic weed, red sanders, prohibited wildlife products, e-cigarettes, foreign-origin poppy seeds and areca nuts. These operations led to the arrest of 20 persons, including 5 foreign nationals, involved in smuggling and trafficking activities and exposed sophisticated concealment techniques employed by organised criminal syndicates.

4 kg gold seized at IGI, Delhi

On 29.07.26, in a significant operation at Indira Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi, officers of DRI intercepted two foreign nationals who had arrived from Dubai. Examination of passenger trolley revealed a specially created secret cavity fabricated using a steel sheet matching the dimensions of the trolley and secured with double-sided adhesive tapes. The cavity yielded 40 foreign-origin gold bars weighing 4 kg. The gold was seized and both passengers were arrested.

Previously in the week, in separate operations conducted jointly by DRI and Border Security Force personnel along the Indo-Bangladesh border, officers seized around 3.2 kg of foreign-origin gold. The gold was recovered from a person near the border fence at Tungi, another person at Hili border gate, and in a third case from a person at motorcycle intercepted near Nityanandakati, Hakimpur. Three persons including a woman were arrested in connection with the seizures.

In addition to above cases, DRI officers also seized around 2.2 kg of gold in three different operations conducted at Varanasi, Delhi Airport and Tamil Naidu and arrested 4 persons.

In total, around 9.5 kg gold valued at around Rs. 14 crore was seized and 9 persons arrested.

Wildlife products

In a significant case involving prohibited imports, officers of DRI uncovered an attempt to import around 14 metric tonnes of Pakistan-origin Guggul resin valued at Rs. 1.4 crore approx. through misdeclaration of description and country of origin. The consignment, had been falsely declared as natural resin originating from Somalia and routed through Dubai.

Guggul resin (Commiphora resin), a species endemic to the arid regions of India and Pakistan is listed in CITES Appendix II and is categorised as Critically Endangered in the IUCN Red list. Investigation established that the consignment was Guggul resin and was of Pakistan origin and had been trans-shipped using forged documentation. The import is in violation of DGFT restrictions prohibiting direct or indirect import of goods originating in or exported from Pakistan. Two persons involved in the conspiracy were arrested

In another major wildlife and forest produce smuggling case, officers of DRI intercepted a truck on the outskirts of Chennai and recovered 142 red sanders logs weighing around 4.8 metric tonnes, concealed behind empty plastic crates. Red Sanders is a protected species listed under Appendix II of CITES and covered under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The seized consignment is valued at approximately Rs 2.50 crore. Investigation revealed the involvement of an organised smuggling network with a history of illicit exports. Three persons were arrested.

In Manipur, acting on specific intelligence regarding cross-border narcotics trafficking from Myanmar, officers of DRI, with assistance from Assam Rifles and Manipur Police, intercepted a vehicle near Churachandpur and recovered around 2.7 kg heroin concealed inside 220 soap cases. Two persons were arrested.

In two other operations in Mumbai, DRI officers intercepted two foreign female nationals travelling from Delhi and recovered synthetic narcotic drugs concealed in specially fabricated cavities in their respective baggage. The operations resulted in the collective seizure of around 2 kg Amphetamine crystals and MDMA tablets . Both passengers were arrested

under the NDPS Act, 1985.

Seized MDMA tablets & Amphetamine crystals

In two different operations, at Indira Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi and Calicut International Airport, DRI officers intercepted two passengers including a foreign nationals around 25 kg hydroponic weed from their possession was seized. Both passengers had travelled from Bangkok and were arrested.

Tobacco products

In another operation aimed at curbing the illicit import of prohibited goods, officers of DRI intercepted an import consignment at Nhava Sheva Port that had been mis-declared as LED lights and fixtures and recovered 9,230 prohibited electronic cigarettes of various brands and flavours. Electronic cigarettes are prohibited in India under the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019. The prohibited e-cigarettes along with the cover cargo, having a total value of approximately Rs 3.70 crore, were seized.

E-cigarette seized at Mumbai

Restricted items

In Mizoram, officers of DRI, assisted by Assam Rifles personnel, searched four suspected godowns near the Indo-Myanmar border and recovered around 14.5 MT of poppy seeds and 14 MT areca nuts, both of foreign origin collectively valued at around Rs 3.6 crore. Preliminary investigation indicates that the goods had been smuggled into India through the Zokhawthar sector of the Indo-Myanmar border. The goods were seized under the Customs Act, 1962.

Poppy seeds are classified as a "Restricted" item under the Foreign Trade Policy and its imports is permitted only subject to specified conditions, including import of legally cultivated produce from designated countries and mandatory registration of all import contracts with the Narcotics Commissioner, Gwalior.

Review Committees of the Railway Board, Ministry of Railways have recommended premature retirement of five Group 'A' officers in public interest under Rule 1802(a) of the Indian Railway Establishment Code, Volume II, which is equivalent to Rule 56(j) of the Fundamental Rules.

The Review Committees have recommended premature retirement of two SAG officers of IRHS, one JAG officer of IRSE in Northern Railway, one officer of IRSEE in Northern Railway, and one JAG officer of IRTS in Western Railway.

The Review Committees carried out a detailed assessment of the officers' service records in accordance with the prescribed procedure. The review included examination of Annual Performance Appraisal Reports (APARs), integrity records, vigilance inputs, disciplinary history and other relevant service records before arriving at their recommendations. The committees unanimously recommended premature retirement of the officers in public interest in the respective cases.

Indian Railways follows a policy of zero tolerance towards corruption, lack of integrity and inefficiency. Integrity, discipline and accountability in public service remain non-negotiable. Actions taken under the relevant provisions of the Indian Railway Establishment Code are aimed at upholding these core values.

headline: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi lays the foundation stone, inaugurates and dedicates to the nation multiple development projects worth over ₹17,900 crore in Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh
fullText:

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi lays the foundation stone, inaugurates and dedicates to the nation multiple development projects worth over ₹17,900 crore in Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh

Today's projects across aviation, clean energy, semiconductors and connectivity will contribute to the state's development: PM

On the very land where Alluri Sitarama Raju ji dedicated his life to the welfare of tribal communities; a new airport for Andhra Pradesh is being inaugurated today: PM

This airport serves as the runway for the growth of Andhra and North Andhra, It is a launchpad for a brighter future for the youth of Andhra: PM

It is imperative that Andhra Pradesh and the nation derive maximum benefit from the potential of our talented youth; To achieve this, our focus is currently on futuristic technology industries such as semiconductors, The foundation stone laying ceremony for the new semiconductor plant in Visakhapatnam marks a significant step in this direction: PM

Today, the nation is consistently bolstering its blue economy; Our vision is to develop this entire region as a Coastal Economic Corridor, With this objective in mind, our older ports from Visakhapatnam to Krishnapatnam are being modernized; Additionally, we are constructing new ports in Mulapeta and Ramayapatnam: PM

01 AUG 2026 3:05PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today laid the foundation stone, inaugurated and dedicated to the nation multiple development projects worth over ₹17,900 crore in Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh. Highlighting the immense significance of the day for the Swarna Andhra vision, the Prime Minister expressed profound gratitude for visiting the sacred land of North Andhra during such an auspicious month, offering his deep respects to Lord Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy, Sri Kurmanath Swamy, and Maa Pydithalli Ammavaru. "It is my great privilege to be on the holy land of North Andhra today to witness this momentous occasion,” noted Shri Modi.

Inaugurating and laying the foundation for development projects worth approximately eighteen thousand crore rupees, the Prime Minister emphasized that these multi-sectoral initiatives encompassing airport infrastructure, road connectivity, and energy security perfectly symbolize the state's rapid pace of progress. "These development works are a true symbol of the incredible speed at which Andhra Pradesh is advancing,” observed Shri Modi.

Framing the event as a moment of unprecedented historical significance, the Prime Minister pointed out that alongside monumental infrastructural milestones, the day was equally marked by a spectacular cultural world record achieved through the traditional Dhimsa dance. "Today's event is about creating a new history and setting new records on multiple fronts,” asserted Shri Modi.

Praising the spectacular performance by over thirteen thousand tribal sisters and daughters, the Prime Minister lauded their incredible enthusiasm and discipline, noting that the vibrant display beautifully encapsulated the nation's rich diversity and deeply preserved indigenous heritage. "The pride of our tribal culture displayed here was truly a magnificent and unforgettable sight,” remarked Shri Modi.

Paying tribute to the heroic legacy of Alluri Sitarama Raju and his lifelong dedication to tribal welfare, the Prime Minister described the newly launched airport on this very soil as a critical runway for regional growth and a powerful launchpad for the youth's prosperous future. "Serving as the runway for the growth of Andhra and North Andhra, this airport is the ultimate launchpad for a better future for Andhra's youth," asserted Shri Modi.

Announcing the government's formal decision to name the new aviation facility after the legendary freedom fighter, the Prime Minister expressed confidence that the monumental tribute would instill a profound sense of national duty in every traveler passing through its gates. "Any citizen traveling through this airport will instantly draw inspiration for public and national service from the name of Sri Alluri Sitarama Raju,” asserted Shri Modi.

Outlining the extraordinary transformation of the civil aviation sector over the past twelve years, the Prime Minister contrasted the meager seventy-four operational airports in 2014 with the current count of one hundred and sixty-six, celebrating the democratization of air travel for ordinary citizens from smaller cities under the current administration. "Today, the common people of small cities are comfortably traveling by flights, marking a departure from when air travel was restricted to large metropolises,” observed Shri Modi.

Crediting the UDAN scheme for fundamentally shifting the aviation landscape, the Prime Minister highlighted how the initiative has successfully enabled impoverished families to realize their flying dreams, further detailing the recent launch of its second phase backed by a massive twenty-nine thousand crore rupee investment. "This scheme has actively helped even the poorest of the poor in fulfilling their lifelong dreams,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Pointing to another major milestone in the aviation sector, the Prime Minister referenced the recent rollout of the 'spoke airport' model in Kashi, which has now successfully expanded to Amritsar, dramatically linking the city in Punjab to over twenty-five international destinations. “From this very land of Andhra, I also extend my heartfelt congratulations to the people of Punjab for this achievement,” remarked Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister commended the current leadership under the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister, and is now executing the state's growth agenda at twice the speed. "Our Andhra Pradesh has always possessed the immense capability to become the ultimate growth engine for a Viksit Bharat,” asserted Shri Modi.

Detailing the national strategy to aggressively fortify the Blue Economy, the Prime Minister outlined the ambitious vision of transforming the entire coastal stretch into an integrated economic corridor through the modernization of heritage ports from Visakhapatnam to Krishnapatnam and the construction of new maritime hubs at Mulapeta and Ramayapatnam. "Our strategic vision is to comprehensively develop this entire region as a thriving Coastal Economic Corridor,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Complementing the expansive port developments, the Prime Minister highlighted the rapid construction of a dense highway and expressway network across the state, citing major arteries like the Visakhapatnam-Raipur Expressway as critical catalysts for regional momentum. "These expressway projects are fundamentally imparting unprecedented speed to this entire geographic region,” noted Shri Modi.

Emphasizing the urgent need to seamlessly connect the region with major national industrial hubs, the Prime Minister announced that railway projects worth approximately one lakh crore rupees are currently underway, boasting complete network electrification and the modernization of over seventy stations. "We are actively working to ensure this entire region connects effortlessly with the country's largest industrial centers,” asserted Shri Modi.

Integrating these multi-modal transport upgrades, the Prime Minister underscored the pivotal role of the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan in unifying rail, port, and air infrastructure, which will ultimately optimize logistics, empower local farmers, and significantly boost the ease of doing business. ''Once this modern logistics network is fully ready, it will provide better connectivity to industries and greatly benefit our farmers, and the 'Ease of Doing Business' will also improve” observed Shri Modi.

Praising the state's historical propensity for forward-thinking innovation, the Prime Minister lauded the global dominance of local youth in the software and technology sectors, reiterating the government's steadfast commitment to harnessing this incredible talent pool directly for regional development.

Stressing the absolute necessity of retaining and utilizing this youthful brilliance domestically, the Prime Minister shifted focus toward futuristic tech industries, identifying the foundation laying of the new semiconductor plant in Visakhapatnam as a monumental stride in that specific direction. "Our primary focus is now firmly set on futuristic tech industries like semiconductors to maximize the potential of our talented youth,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Envisioning a transformative industrial shift, the Prime Minister projected that the state will seamlessly transition into a formidable manufacturing hub alongside its software prowess, thereby generating an entirely new ecosystem of futuristic employment opportunities. "This strategic evolution will successfully create futuristic jobs and a brand-new environment for tech industries across the state,” noted Shri Modi.

Explaining the complex mechanics of global economic growth centers, the Prime Minister clarified that solitary factories are insufficient without a comprehensive surrounding ecosystem, a supportive environment that is currently being meticulously crafted in the state thanks to the relentless personal efforts of the Chief Minister. "It is strictly the result of this day-and-night hard work that many large global companies now eagerly want to invest here,” observed Shri Modi.

Expanding on the advanced technological infrastructure, the Prime Minister highlighted concurrent developments in AI and data centers, explicitly mentioning Google's massive fifteen-billion-dollar campus announcement as a clear indicator of the immense global interest that will directly benefit local youth. "Many more global companies are seeing incredible new possibilities here, heavily benefiting the youth of both the state and the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Broadening the scope of the state's industrial narrative beyond digital technology, the Prime Minister pointed to the central government's substantial support for a massive new Pharma Park in Nakkapalli, positioning the state to become a leading national pharmaceutical hub. "With this support, Andhra Pradesh will rapidly develop into one of the country's largest pharma hubs,” asserted Shri Modi.

Turning to the renewable energy sector, the Prime Minister revealed that the Rayalaseema region alone has attracted investments exceeding five lakh crore rupees, offering a firm reassurance to the public regarding the administration's relentless dedication to materializing these ambitious goals. "Our government will continue working day and night to turn every such immense possibility into a solid reality,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Quantifying the sheer velocity of the administration's developmental agenda across all sectors, the Prime Minister reminded the audience of the staggering scale of recent investments, noting the launch of projects worth two lakh crore rupees during his last three visits alone. "You can easily gauge the incredible speed of work across every sector from these massive recent project launches,” noted Shri Modi.

Expressing deep satisfaction over the systematic empowerment of the northern districts within this broader growth narrative, the Prime Minister detailed the strategic evolution of the Visakhapatnam Economic Region (VER) into a premier Asian economic powerhouse, with every new facility contributing to this unified mission. "Our ultimate target is to ensure that the Visakhapatnam Economic Region becomes the most prominent economic hub in Asia,” asserted Shri Modi.

Unpacking the government's core economic philosophy of converting investments directly into employment, the Prime Minister explained the virtuous cycle where increased public and private funding drives manufacturing, bolsters exports, and ultimately elevates household incomes and living standards, exactly as is unfolding in the state today. "When employment increases, people's incomes naturally rise, and the everyday lives of families significantly improve,” observed Shri Modi.

Concluding the address with absolute certainty in the region's bright future, the Prime Minister expressed confidence that the myriad projects initiated during the event would serve as foundational pillars in fulfilling the grand resolutions of both Swarna Andhra and a Viksit Bharat.

Smt Alka Nangia Arora, a 1991-batch officer of the Indian Defence Accounts Service (IDAS), assumed charge as the Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) today, on August 1, 2026.

An alumnus of Garhwal University, Dehradun and IIT Roorkee, Smt Arora has tenanted key appointments in the Government of India, including as Additional Secretary & Financial Adviser in Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) under the Ministry of Agriculture, Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Managing Director of Central Cottage Industries Corporation of India Limited, and Additional Development Commissioner for Handicrafts under the Ministry of Textiles. Smt Arora began her career in the Ministry of Defence at Dum Dum Ordnance Factory in Kolkata, and since then has held key appointments in the Defence Accounts Department (DAD). She has served with all three armed forces, including as FA to Admiral Superintendent of the Naval Dockyard (ASD) in Mumbai, FA to the Army Eastern Command and head of the Area Accounts Office in Kolkata, as IFA to the Western Air Command (WAC) and Army Hospital Research & Referral (AHRR), and Principal IFA to the Air Force Headquarters. The inspection was conducted in presence of the Commissioner, Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), and senior officials of the Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).

During the on-site review, MCD informed the Hon’ble Minister that till 31st July, 2026, 99.07 lakh MT legacy waste has been remediated at Bhalswa dumpsite, and the remaining mound of legacy waste is expected to be cleared by 15 October 2026, while the waste accumulated up to March 2026 is targeted for clearance by 31 December 2026.

The Hon’ble Minister directed MCD that the newly awarded work for processing fresh waste arriving at the Landfill site be expedited, so that the pace of remediation is further accelerated and scientific management of incoming waste is ensured without delay.

The inspection underscores the sustained priority being accorded by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to the time-bound clearance of legacy waste and the comprehensive remediation of the Bhalswa dumpsite.

Text of PM's address at the launch of development projects in Andhra Pradesh

01 AUG 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi

भारत माता की जय।

आंध्र प्रदेश के गवर्नर अब्दुल नज़ीर जी, गोवा के गवर्नर और इस धरती के संतान अशोक गजपति राजू जी, सीएम, मेरे मित्र चंद्रबाबू नायडू जी, डिप्टी सीएम भाई पवन कल्याण जी, मंत्रिमंडल में मेरे साथी युवा ऊर्जा से भरे हुए भाई राममोहन नायडू जी, चंद्रशेखर पेम्मसानी जी, भूपति राजू श्रीनिवास वर्मा जी, राज्य सरकार के मंत्री भाई नारा लोकेश जी, उपस्थित अन्य जनप्रतिनिधिगण, देवियों और सज्जनों।

अंदरिकी नमस्कारम्!

आज का दिन आंध्र प्रदेश के विकास के लिए, स्वर्ण आंध्र के विजन के लिए ये बहुत अहम है। मुझे आज बहुत शुभ अवसर पर, एक शुभ मास में उत्तर आंध्र की इस पवित्र भूमि पर आने का सौभाग्य मिला है। मैं सबसे पहले भगवान श्री वराह लक्ष्मी नरसिंह स्वामी के चरणों में प्रणाम करता हूं। मैं श्री-कूर्मनाथ स्वामी और मां पैडितल्ली अम्मवारु को नमन करता हूं।

आज यहां करीब Eighteen Thousand Crore Rupees की विकास परियोजनाओं का शुभारंभ, लोकार्पण और शिलान्यास हुआ है। एयरपोर्ट के साथ साथ ये प्रोजेक्ट्स आंध्र की रोड कनेक्टिविटी से भी जुड़े हैं। इनमें एनर्जी सिक्योरिटी से जुड़े प्रोजेक्ट्स भी हैं। ये विकास कार्य इस बात के प्रतीक हैं कि इस समय आंध्र किस स्पीड से आगे बढ़ रहा है। मैं आप सभी को इन प्रोजेक्ट्स की बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं देता हूं।

आज का ये आयोजन नया इतिहास, नए record, इसे रचने का भी है। आज एक ओर विकास के नए रिकॉर्ड बन रहे हैं, तो साथ ही धीमसा डांस का सांस्कृतिक record भी रचा गया है, और ये चंद्रबाबू की विशेषता है कि उन्होंने दो क्षितिजों को छुआ है। एक तरफ ऊंची आसमान को छूने वाली व्यवस्था एयरपोर्ट का निर्माण और दूसरी तरफ मेरे यहां के आदिवासी बहनों के द्वारा धीमसा नृत्य का विश्व रिकॉर्ड बनाना, मैं चंद्रबाबू के इस विजन को विशेषरूप से सराहना करता हूं।

Thirteen Thousand से ज्यादा आदिवासी बहनों और बेटियों की प्रस्तुति, उनका उत्साह, उनका अनुशासन और आदिवासी संस्कृति का गौरव, ये दृश्य वाकई अद्भुत था। इसमें देश की विविधता की झलक भी थी और पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी सहेजकर रखी गई जनजातीय विरासत भी थी। मैं इस प्रस्तुति के लिए आप सभी का और विशेष रूप से मेरी आदिवासी बहनों और बेटियों का बहुत-बहुत अभिनंदन करता हूं।

ये धरती अल्लूरी सीताराम राजू की धरती है। अल्लूरी सीताराम राजू जी ने जिस धरती पर आदिवासी हितों के लिए अपना जीवन समर्पित किया, आज उसी धरती पर आंध्र प्रदेश के एक नए एयरपोर्ट की शुरुआत हो रही है। ये एयरपोर्ट आंध्र और उत्तर आंध्र की ग्रोथ का रन-वे है। ये आंध्र के युवाओं के बेहतर भविष्य का लॉंन्च पैड है। मैं आंध्र प्रदेश के लोगों को, देश के लोगों को बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं।

पहले जब एयरपोर्ट बनते थे, तो एयरपोर्ट के नाम एक ही परिवार के नाम पर चढ़ जाते थे, हमने इस परंपरा को बदला, हमने अयोध्या में एयरपोर्ट का नाम वाल्मीकि के नाम से जोड़ा, हमने पंजाब में संत रविदास जी के नाम से एयरपोर्ट का नाम जोड़ा।

केंद्र की एनडीए सरकार ने ये निर्णय़ किया है कि इस नए एयरपोर्ट का नाम श्री अल्लूरी सीताराम राजू के नाम पर होगा। आंध्र प्रदेश का जो भी नागरिक, इस एयरपोर्ट से यात्रा करेगा, देश और दुनिया का जो भी नागरिक इस एयरपोर्ट से यात्रा करेगा, उसे अल्लूरी सीताराम राजू जी के नाम से जनसेवा और राष्ट्रसेवा की प्रेरणा मिलेगी।

बीते twelve years में देश के एविएशन सेक्टर ने असाधारण प्रगति की है। 2014 तक देश में केवल Seventy Four एयरपोर्ट ऑपरेशनल थे। आज ये संख्या One Hundred Sixty Six है। एक समय था जब हवाई उड़ानें सिर्फ बड़े शहरों तक सीमित थीं। NDA सरकार में आज छोटे शहरे के साधारण लोग भी फ्लाइट्स से आ-जा रहे हैं। Twelve years में सिर्फ एयरपोर्ट की संख्या ही नहीं बढ़ी है, हमारी उड़ान योजना के काऱण आज गरीब परिवार के लोगों को भी जहाज में बैठने का अवसर मिल रहा है। इस योजना ने गरीब से गरीब को अपना सपना पूरा करने में मदद की है। कुछ दिन पहले ही सरकार ने उड़ान योजना के दूसरे फेज की शुरुआत की है। इस पर भी Twenty Nine Thousand करोड़ रुपीज खर्च किए जाएंगे।

एविएशन सेक्टर में देश ने एक और बड़ा माइलस्टोन हासिल किया है। कुछ ही दिन पहले काशी में जिस स्पोक एयरपोर्ट मॉडल का शुभारंभ हुआ, आज वही मॉडल पंजाब के अमृतसर तक पहुँच गया है। इससे अमृतसर से Twenty Five से ज्यादा इंटरनेशनल डेस्टिनेशन जुड़ जाएंगे। मैं इस उपलब्धि के लिए आंध्र की इस धरती से पंजाब के लोगों को भी बधाई देता हूँ।

हमारे आंध्र प्रदेश के पास हमेशा से विकसित भारत का ग्रोथ इंजन बनने का सामर्थ्य रहा है। आंध्र प्रदेश के विकास के लिए हमारे प्रयास डबल इंजन की स्पीड से आगे बढ़ें, इसके लिए मैंने आंध्र के लोगों से डबल इंजन सरकार का आशीर्वाद मांगा था और आज चंद्रबाबू नायडू जी के नेतृत्व में, पवन कल्याण जी के नेतृत्व में NDA की पूरी टीम आंध्र प्रदेश के लिए डबल स्पीड से काम कर रही है।

आज देश ब्लू इकोनॉमी को लगातार मजबूत कर रहा है। हमारा विज़न है कि ये पूरा क्षेत्र कोस्टल इकोनॉमिक कॉरिडोर के रूप में विकसित हो, इसी लक्ष्य के साथ विशाखापट्टनम से कृष्णापट्टनम तक हमारे पुराने पोर्ट्स को आधुनिक रूप दिया जा रहा है। इसके अलावा मुलापेटा और रामायापट्टनम में हम नए पोर्ट्स भी बना रहे हैं।

पोर्ट डेवलपमेंट के साथ-साथ पूरे आंध्र में हाइवे और एक्सप्रेसवे का नेटवर्क तैयार हो रहा है। विशाखापट्टनम-रायपुर एक्सप्रेसवे जैसे प्रोजेक्ट इस पूरे क्षेत्र को रफ्तार दे रहे हैं।

ये पूरा रीजन देश के बड़े औद्योगिक केंद्रों से आसानी से जुड़े इसके लिए आज आंध्र प्रदेश में करीब one lakh crore रुपीज की रेलवे परियोजनाओं पर काम चल रहा है। राज्य के पूरे रेल नेटवर्क का electrification हो चुका है। यहां Seventy से ज्यादा रेलवे स्टेशनों को भी आधुनिक बनाया जा रहा है।

आज इस क्षेत्र के विकास में पीएम गति शक्ति नेशनल मास्टर प्लान भी बड़ी भूमिका निभा रहा है। पीएम गति शक्ति के माध्यम से इस पूरे क्षेत्र में रेल, पोर्ट और एयरपोर्ट को एक साथ जोड़ा जा रहा है। जब यहां ये आधुनिक लॉजिस्टिक्स नेटवर्क तैयार हो जाएगा, तो उद्योगों को बेहतर कनेक्टिविटी मिलेगी, किसानों को फायदा होगा और Ease of Doing Business भी बढ़ेगा।

आंध्र प्रदेश हमेशा भविष्य की सोच रखने वाला प्रदेश रहा है। सॉफ्टवेयर, IT और टेक सेक्टर में आंध्र के युवाओं ने पूरी दुनिया में अपना डंका बजाया है। और इसीलिए, सरकार यहां के टैलेंट को, आंध्र प्रदेश की डेवलपमेंट पावर से जोड़ना चाहती है। हमारे टैलेंटेड युवाओं की प्रतिभा का लाभ आंध्र प्रदेश और देश को ज्यादा से ज्यादा मिले, ये बहुत आवश्यक है। इसके लिए हमारा फोकस अब सेमीकंडक्टर जैसी futuristic टेक इंडस्ट्री पर है। विशाखापट्टनम में नए सेमीकंडक्टर प्लांट का शिलान्यास, इसी दिशा में एक बहुत बड़ा कदम है। चंद्रबाबू के नेतृत्व में हमारा आंध्र अब सॉफ्टवेयर के साथ-साथ manufacturing का भी हब बनेगा। इससे आंध्र में futuristic jobs तैयार होगी, टेक इंडस्ट्रीज़ के लिए नया वातावरण तैयार होगा।

वर्ल्ड इकोनॉमी में कहीं भी, किसी भी ग्रोथ सेंटर का निर्माण सिर्फ एक फैक्ट्री से नहीं हो सकता, उसके लिए एक पूरे इकोसिस्टम की जरूरत होती है। आज आंध्र प्रदेश में हम ग्रोथ का वही इकोसिस्टम तैयार कर रहे हैं। चंद्रबाबू नायडू जी व्यक्तिगत स्तर पर दिन-रात मेहनत करते हैं। इसी का परिणाम है, आज दुनिया की कई बड़ी-बड़ी कंपनियां यहाँ निवेश करने के लिए आना चाहती हैं।

यहां सेमीकंडक्टर के साथ-साथ AI इन्फ्रा और डेटा सेंटर पर भी काम हो रहा है। Google ने भी यहां Fifteen Billion Dollars के AI और क्लाउड इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर कैंपस की घोषणा की है। और भी कई ग्लोबल कंपनीज यहां नई संभावनाएं देख रही हैं। इसका बहुत बड़ा फायदा आंध्र प्रदेश के साथ-साथ देश के Youth को हो रहा है।

आंध्र की इंडस्ट्रियल ग्रोथ स्टोरी केवल डिजिटल टेक तक ही सीमित नहीं है। नक्कापल्ली में केंद्र सरकार बड़े फार्मा पार्क के लिए भी सहयोग दे रही है। इससे आंध्र प्रदेश, देश के एक बड़े फार्मा हब के रूप में भी विकसित होगा। ग्रीन एनर्जी की फील्ड में भी अकेले रायलसीमा क्षेत्र में Five Lakh Crore Rupees से ज्यादा का इनवेस्टमेंट हुआ है। मैं आज आंध्र प्रदेश के आप सभी लोगों को फिर विश्वास दिलाता हूं, हमारी सरकार ऐसी हर संभावनाओं को साकार करने के लिए दिन-रात, ये डबल इंजन सरकार काम करती रहेगी।

आज आंध्र प्रदेश में हर सेक्टर में किस स्पीड से काम हो रहा है, इसका अंदाजा आप इस बात से लगा सकते हैं कि पिछली 3 यात्राओं में ही मैंने Two Lakh Crore Rupees के प्रोजेक्ट्स का शुभारंभ यहाँ किया है। मुझे खुशी है कि आंध्र की इस विकास यात्रा में ‘उत्तर आंध्र’ भी सशक्त हो रहा है। हम Visakhapatnam Economic Region, V.E.R को देश के बड़े औद्योगिक केंद्र के रूप में विकसित कर रहे हैं। हमारा लक्ष्य है, V.E.R एशिया का प्रमुख economic hub बने। ये एयरपोर्ट से लेकर सेमीकंडक्टर यूनिट तक इसी मिशन का हिस्सा है।

हमारी सरकार का मंत्र है- Investment से Employment, इसलिए सरकार ने अपनी तरफ से भी Investment बढ़ाया है और हम प्राइवेट सेक्टर को भी Investment के लिए प्रेरित कर रहे हैं। आप भी जानते हैं, जब Investment बढ़ता है, तो मैन्युफैक्चरिंग बढ़ती है, मैन्युफैक्चरिंग बढ़ती है, तो एक्सपोर्ट बढ़ता है, एक्सपोर्ट बढ़ता है, तो रोजगार के नए अवसर बनते हैं और रोजगार बढ़ता है, तो लोगों की आमदनी बढ़ती है, परिवारों की ज़िंदगी बेहतर होती है और आंध्र प्रदेश में हम यही होते देख रहे हैं।

मुझे पूरा विश्वास है, आज यहां जितने भी प्रोजेक्ट्स की शुरुआत हुई हैं, जिनकी नींव रखी गई हैं, वो सारे प्रोजेक्ट्स स्वर्ण आंध्रा और विकसित भारत के संकल्प को पूरा करने में बहुत बड़ा योगदान देंगे। चंद्रबाबू जी के नेतृत्व में आंध्र प्रदेश विकसित भारत के सपने को पूरा करने के लिए एक बहुत बड़ा ऊर्जा स्रोत बन रहा है। मैं एक बार फिर इन सभी परियोजनाओं के लिए आंध्र प्रदेश के लोगों को बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूँ।

headline: INDIAN ARMY BIDS FAREWELL TO GENERAL VN SHARMA, FORMER CHIEF OF THE ARMY STAFF, WITH FULL MILITARY HONOURS
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

INDIAN ARMY BIDS FAREWELL TO GENERAL VN SHARMA, FORMER CHIEF OF THE ARMY STAFF, WITH FULL MILITARY HONOURS

01 AUG 2026 2:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Army paid its final tribute to General Vishwa Nath Sharma (Retired), PVSM, AVSM, ADC, a former Chief of the Army Staff. His last rites were conducted with full military honours today at Brar Square Crematorium, New Delhi. General Sharma passed away yesterday morning in New Delhi at the age of 97.

General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Army Staff, on behalf of all ranks of the Indian Army, laid a wreath and offered his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family. General VK Singh (Retired), Governor of Mizoram and former Chief of the Army Staff, also laid a wreath and attended the funeral. The solemn ceremony was attended by the former Chief of Defence Staff, former Chiefs of the Army Staff, the Chief of the Air Staff, the Chief of the Naval Staff, serving and retired senior military officers, veterans and family members, who gathered to pay their final respects to the distinguished soldier.

General Sharma was born in London, United Kingdom, on 4 June 1930. He was the younger brother of Major Somnath Sharma, recipient of India’s first Param Vir Chakra, and of Lt Gen Surendra Nath Sharma, former Engineer-in-Chief of the Indian Army.

He joined the Indian Military Academy, Dehradun, as part of the 5th Regular Course and was commissioned into 16 Light Cavalry on 4 June 1950. He joined 66 Armoured Regiment as Second-in-Command at the time of its raising on 01 September 1966 and assumed command of the Regiment in June 1968 as its second Commandant, relinquishing command in February 1970.

Through his career, General Sharma held various staff appointments including Colonel General Staff of an Armoured Division, Brigadier General Staff of a Corps, Director General of Military Operations at Army Headquarters and Commandant of the College of Combat (now Army War College), Mhow. He commanded a Mountain Brigade in Mizoram, an Armoured Brigade in Jaipur, a Mountain Division in Sikkim, a Corps in Mizoram and Eastern Command in Kolkata, prior to taking over as Chief of the Army Staff from 30 April 1988 to 30 June 1990. General Sharma was the recipient of numerous distinguished awards during his professional career.

Post his retirement, continuing the philanthropic legacy of both his father and father-in-law, General Sharma dedicated four decades to serving underprivileged communities through a free tuberculosis clinic in Himachal Pradesh. Travelling by ambulance to remote villages and often trekking to high-altitude settlements alongside his medical team, he brought essential healthcare to people with limited access to medical services. His unwavering commitment to compassionate service inspired future generations of the family, with his son and other relatives carrying forward this tradition of public service.

General Sharma’s life of distinguished service, courage and dedication to the Nation will continue to inspire generations of soldiers.

headline: Ministry of Textiles to celebrate 12th National Handloom Day on 7 August 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Textiles

Ministry of Textiles to celebrate 12th National Handloom Day on 7 August 2026

Hon'ble President Smt. Droupadi Murmu to grace the celebrations as the Chief Guest

01 AUG 2026 2:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Textiles will celebrate the 12th National Handloom Day on 7 August 2026 with a national function at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre (RBCC), New Delhi, to celebrate India's rich handloom heritage and recognise the contribution of the handloom weaving community to the nation's cultural and economic development

The Hon'ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, will grace the occasion as the Chief Guest. The function will also be attended by the Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh, Union Minister of State for Textiles Shri Pabitra Margherita, Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary (Textiles) and Dr. M. Beena, Development Commissioner (Handlooms).

The celebrations will be attended by Sant Kabir Handloom Awardees and National Handloom Awardees and their family members, handloom weavers from across the country, members of the Awards Selection Committee, eminent personalities associated with the handloom sector, senior Government officials, media representatives and other distinguished guests.

A major highlight of the celebrations will be the presentation of the Sant Kabir Handloom Awards and the National Handloom Awards for the year 2025. A total of 22 awards, comprising 03 Sant Kabir Handloom Awards and 19 National Handloom Awards, will be conferred upon outstanding handloom weavers for their outstanding craftsmanship, innovation and contribution to the preservation of India's handloom traditions.

The occasion will also witness the release of four commemorative postage stamps celebrating India's rich and diverse handloom weaving traditions.

Two publications—"Earth. Root. Thread – Aal Dyed Handloom Textiles of Central India" and the Handloom Awards Book 2025—will also be unveiled during the function.

An exhibition showcasing award-winning handloom products will be organised on the sidelines of the event. Visitors will also have an opportunity to witness live demonstrations of traditional Kani weaving and Wall Hanging weaving, providing a glimpse into the diversity and craftsmanship of India's handloom traditions.

In addition to the main function on 7th August, 2026, other significant events planned around the National Handloom Day include exhibitions, conclaves (designer, IIHT) etc.

India's handloom sector continues to be one of the country's largest sources of sustainable rural employment, supporting the livelihoods of more than 35 lakh persons, with women constituting over 70 per cent of the workforce. Besides its economic significance, the sector remains a custodian of India's rich textile traditions and an important contributor to environmentally sustainable production practices.

National Handloom Day is observed every year on 7 August to commemorate the Swadeshi Movement launched on 7 August 1905, which gave renewed impetus to indigenous industries and India's handloom sector. The observance recognises the enduring contribution of handloom weavers to the country's cultural heritage and socio-economic development.

Since its inception in 2015, National Handloom Day has served as an occasion to celebrate the artistry, skill and dedication of India's handloom weavers while reaffirming the Government's commitment to the preservation, promotion and sustainable development of the handloom sector.

headline: Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav presides over the Convocation Ceremony of 2024 batch of Indian Forest Service (IFS) Probationers at Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy; Presents Certificates and Medals as the Chief Guest
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav presides over the Convocation Ceremony of 2024 batch of Indian Forest Service (IFS) Probationers at Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy; Presents Certificates and Medals as the Chief Guest

The young officers passing out today will lead the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047: Shri Bhupender Yadav

A good officer is one who is first and foremost a good human being: Shri Bhupender Yadav

A total of 111 officers, including 109 Indian Forest Service probationers and two officer trainees from Bhutan, completed the 20-month training programme

Ms. Pratiksha Nanasaheb Kale of the Rajasthan Cadre emerged as the batch topper

01 AUG 2026 1:26PM by PIB Dehradun

The Convocation Ceremony of the 2024 Batch Indian Forest Service (IFS) probationers undergoing training at the Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy (IGNFA), Dehradun, was held on Saturday at the Convocation Hall of the Forest Research Institute (FRI). Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, presided over the ceremony as the Chief Guest and presented certificates and medals to the successful probationers.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Yadav congratulated the officers on successfully completing their training and said that they had received outstanding technical and leadership training at one of the country's premier academies. He expressed confidence that when these officers reach the most productive phase of their careers, India will be celebrating 100 years of Independence and they will play a significant role in achieving and leading the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Union minister said that the officers would face major challenges in the coming years, including climate change, biodiversity loss and desertification. He said addressing these challenges would require equal emphasis on innovation, modern technology and people's participation. He added that artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies should be used not only for data collection and analysis but also for developing practical solutions with human sensitivity.

Shri Yadav said that ethics and efficiency are the strongest foundations of a successful public servant. High moral values, effective utilisation of time and the ability to deliver maximum outcomes with limited resources define the true identity of an officer. He urged the officers to aspire not only to become capable administrators but also effective leaders, stating that sacrifice, compassion and the ability to inspire others are the qualities that distinguish a true leader. Leadership, he said, is not merely about administration but about bringing positive transformation to society.

Concluding his address, the Union Minister said that a good officer is one who is first and foremost a good human being. He urged the officers to make self-assessment and self-awareness an integral part of their lives, adding that every officer's journey after training would be unique and that they should continue learning from their experiences while making exemplary contributions to society and the nation. He also extended his best wishes to all the trainees and their family members.

Earlier, Director, IGNFA, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Khajuria presented the Director's Report and stated that the institution, which began as the Indian Forest College and now functions as the Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy, has been serving the nation since 1938. He informed that all Indian Forest Service officers of independent India, along with 369 forest officers from 14 friendly countries, have received training from the institution. He further stated that under the revised curriculum aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, a total of 111 officers, comprising 109 Indian Forest Service probationers of the 2024 Batch and two officer trainees from Bhutan, completed the 20-month training programme. Of these, 75 officers secured more than 75 per cent marks and were awarded the Honours Diploma.

The Director further informed that the training programme placed special emphasis on forestry, wildlife management, environmental governance, advanced technologies and leadership development, in addition to classroom learning. Nearly 45 per cent of the total training period was devoted to field exercises, study tours and adventure activities across diverse ecological regions of the country.

The probationers also participated in specialised elective courses, independent research and practical exercises related to forest management and wildlife conservation with guidance from eminent experts and support from leading institutions. He urged the passing-out officers to serve with complete dedication towards conserving natural resources and improving the livelihoods of forest-dependent communities.

During the ceremony, awards and medals were presented to probationers for their outstanding achievements. Ms. Pratiksha Nanasaheb Kale of the Rajasthan Cadre emerged as the batch topper.

The ceremony was attended by Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Tanmay Kumar; Director General of Forests and Special Secretary, Shri Sushil Kumar Awasthi; Chairman, CEC, Shri C.P. Goyal; Additional Director General of Forests, Shri Santosh Tiwari; Additional Director General of Forests, Shri Ramesh Kumar Pandey; Additional Secretary, Shri Amandeep Garg; Director General, ICFRE, Smt. Kanchan Devi; Director, IGNFA, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Khajuria; Additional Director, IGNFA, Shri N.C. Saravanan; Inspector General of Forests, Dr. V. Clement Ben; Director, Wildlife Institute of India, Dr. G.S. Bhardwaj; Director, FRI, along with several senior officers, heads of forestry and other institutions based in Dehradun, faculty members and staff of IGNFA and the Central Academy for State Forest Service, retired Indian Forest Service officers, senior officers from the Central and State Governments, trainee officers of the 2025 Batch, and family members of the passing-out officers of the 2024 Batch.
